scenario: WIBTA for testing my boyfriend? | So a short backstory on me, I am a model. And with that most of my previous relationships stem from the guys I am dating on really dating me because of my looks and the "status symbol" of dating a model not because of me as a person. This is something that has caused a lot of anxiety and depression in my life and I have been really trying to find people in my life that care about me not what I look like. Now that is not to say that my looks can't play a role (physical attraction is important to me as well) but I can't be with anyone where that is the only or main reason why they are dating me. So that brings me to a guy a started dating fairly recently. I really like him and he seems like a good guy. Takes interest in my hobbies and is supportive of what I do. He enjoys lazy days around the house and cooking for me at home instead of always wanting to go out (which with a lot of guys it just seemed like they wanted to show me off). So I really really like him. But his friend DM'd me the other day and told me, "Hey, just thought you should know. You boyfriend has been telling anyone who will listen about all the dirty shit he gets to do with 'this model chick I have been banging'. I'd want to know. Hope for the best!" I have only met this guy once and I don't know how close he is to my boyfriend nor do I know why he told me this. For all I know he is just trying to start drama. The problem is I know how badly I want to believe my boyfriend. And if he were to tell me that it isn't true I would probably believe him. But that thought of "what if" would constantly be in my head from now on. So would I be an asshole if for the next month or so I stop wearing makeup when we go out and I don't put out at all (just come up with whatever excuse I need to when he starts trying to make a move)? If I test what his motives truly are? Part of me feels like this is wrong but the other part knows this is the only way I can fully 100% put this behind me. And if his friend is lying I can commit to him 100%

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for this person to test their boyfriend by changing their appearance and behavior. Let me break this down step by step. First, the person is a model, and they've had past relationships where guys were interested in them mainly because of their looks or the status of dating a model. This has caused them a lot of anxiety and depression, so they're really trying to find someone who cares about them as a person, not just their looks. That makes sense because feeling valued for who you are is important in a relationship. Now, they've started dating someone new who seems to be different. He takes interest in their hobbies, supports what they do, likes lazy days at home, and cooks for them instead of always wanting to go out. This is a good sign because it shows he's interested in getting to know them beyond just their looks. But then, his friend DMs them and says that the boyfriend has been bragging about "dirty shit" he gets to do with "this model chick." This is concerning because it suggests that the boyfriend might still be focused on the physical aspect or using their status as a model. The person doesn't know how close the friend is to the boyfriend or why he told them this, so there's uncertainty about whether the friend is truthful or just trying to stir drama. The person is torn because they want to believe their boyfriend, but the doubt is lingering. They're considering testing him by not wearing makeup and not being physically intimate for a month to see if his interest remains. They're questioning if this is wrong or not. On one hand, they want to ensure that their boyfriend is genuinely interested in them as a person and not just for their looks or status. Testing him could help them feel more secure and confident in the relationship. On the other hand, this approach might come across as manipulative or unfair to the boyfriend, who might not even be aware of the friend's comments or might have been taken out of context. I think it's important to consider communication in this situation. Instead of testing him through behavior changes, maybe talking openly with the boyfriend about their concerns would be more effective. This way, both parties can address the issue directly and work towards understanding each other better. However, if the person feels that they can't trust the boyfriend without some form of reassurance, testing might seem like a necessary step. But it's crucial to approach this in a way that's respectful and doesn't damage the relationship unnecessarily. In conclusion, while the intention behind testing is understandable, it might not be the most effective or respectful approach. Open communication and building trust through dialogue could be a healthier way to address these concerns.
